chapter: Advice to youth and the art of drumming
title: Advice to young musicians: learn the whole craft
summary: He urges players to learn all related instruments, pointing to Woody Herman's band using bassoon, bass clarinet and piccolo trumpet.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: What advice would you give a young musician about going into the music business today?

Well, the advice that I would give them is to learn as much about their craft as they possibly can. The reeds instrument, learn all of the reeds, the woodwinds, and if he's a brass -- I saw Woody Herman's band -- I don't know if you saw the big bands over the weekend?
And I noticed the instrumentation that he was using, I mean, the instruments that he was using, like the bassoon, and a bass clarinet, the piccolo trumpet --

Right, right, right. See, so it shows, the thoroughness of the musicians. And they're incorporating these instruments, which were more or less classical instruments before, into the jazz scene. Well, as

you know, jazz moves and it's just like a circle. It just goes around and around. It never stops. There's always something new, and this is what these guys are doing, and they're very refreshing and beautiful sounds.
